title: Continuous scene flow (no page break per scene)
how: saturation sheets run continuously with no forced break between scenes

title: Centered dialogue column, % geometry
why: renderer geometry every page exercises equally: no content could single it out. On the device checklist as a free look, and pinned by the CSS tests

title: Cue & parenthetical alignment (option, default centered)
how: leading, mid-speech and stacked parentheticals under centered cues

title: Vertical rhythm between elements
why: renderer spacing, exercised identically by any content; the CSS tests own it

title: Relative-unit scaling (principle, not an option)
why: a principle, not a content behavior. No PDF content could exercise it

title: Scene heading keeps its context (keep-with-next chain)
how: 15 scene headings, several landing near page seams across the saturation run

title: Mini-slugs, micro-headings not scenes
how: two mini-slugs inside a scene, asserted to type as mini-slug and to stay out of the scene list

title: Keep-with-next, minimal chain (v2)
how: the saturation run puts cue/speech chains against page seams repeatedly

title: Typeface & line height (v2)
why: renderer typography, identical for all content; on the device checklist as a free look

title: Body text alignment, ragged-right by default
how: long action and dialogue paragraphs throughout, where justification would open visible gaps

title: Transitions never begin a page
how: CUT TO:, DISSOLVE TO: and SMASH CUT TO: at right-flush indent, asserted to type as transition

title: Print split minimums (option, default ON)
how: 40 numbered speeches cycling 1/2/4/3 lines so breaks land inside speeches, not only between them

title: Right-margin revision stars, dropped
how: star-only items past 80% page width, which must not survive as action elements

title: (MORE) / (CONT'D) page-break rejoin
how: the MORE-ANCHOR speech is placed at line 44 so it straddles the sheet boundary

title: (CONT'D) normalization (option, default auto)
how: a WREN (CONT'D) cue carrying its extension

title: Cue keeps its first dialogue line (always on)
how: 40 cue/speech pairs against page seams; also the defect speech 37 exposed

title: Whole-speech keep (option, default OFF)
why: OFF by default, so the committed fixture never exercises it. Needs a second conversion with keepSpeechesWhole ON: the only registry entry still carrying a pending device verdict

title: Page furniture stripping
how: printed page numbers on every sheet, which must type as page-number and stay out of the body

title: Final Draft double-print dedup
why: the artifact is exact-coordinate overlapping duplicate items, which this generator cannot emit: it writes each run once. Reproducing it would mean modelling a Final Draft bug rather than a screenplay

title: Dual-margin scene numbers collapsed
how: a heading printing 42 at both margins, asserted to attach as sceneNumber and leave the text clean

title: Hybrid character cues
how: BUNNY (V.O.), name and extension on one cue line

title: Width-aware item joining
how: wrapped action and dialogue throughout, which must rejoin into single elements rather than per-line fragments

title: Inline bold/italic/underline pass-through
how: bold, italic and bold-italic runs in action and dialogue, a run crossing a wrap boundary, and a punctuation-only styled item; plus a drawn underline asserted to reach styledText, and three drawn rules (strikethrough, table border, page-wide rule) asserted NOT to

title: Cue extensions tolerate a missing closing period
how: (O.S.) with its period alongside (V.O) and (O.C) without

title: Cue rescue from the character roster
how: a recurring cast of four, so the roster exists for the rescue pass to draw on

title: Dual dialogue, de-interleaved to sequential speeches
how: a short exchange with both cues sharing one Y, asserted to de-interleave into left speech then right with no element mixing the columns

title: Tall dual exchanges degrade to sequential
how: a second exchange whose taller column passes the 12-line threshold, so the table falls back to sequential speeches

title: Generated title page
how: an invented title, credit and author, asserted to stay out of the character roster

title: Scene-level TOC
how: 15 scenes across the fixture, enough for a TOC with real structure

title: Shooting-script scene numbers, kept in Fountain, hidden in EPUB
how: the 42 dual-margin number, which must serialize into the fountain and not render in the heading

title: Original page-number markers (option, default off)
how: printed page numbers on every sheet are the furniture this option re-surfaces when enabled

title: Scanned-PDF bail-out
why: a screenplay fixture cannot also be a page with no text layer. blank-pages.pdf owns this

title: Not-a-screenplay guard
why: a screenplay fixture cannot also be a non-screenplay. prose.pdf owns this

title: Block font shifts
how: a chyron action block in Helvetica, three inserts at 10/15/18pt covering -1/+1/+2, and a dialogue line in the second face; each asserted to emit the exact [[fmt: ...]] note, and the rest of the fixture asserted to emit none

title: Pictures recognised, recorded as notes
how: five pictures, of which the book must keep exactly four. The title card behind the title sheet (522x702pt, 75.6% of the sheet, so full-page), the storyboard panel on sheet 14 (180pt, 42% of the text column), the map plate under its heading on sheet 15 (558x666pt, 76.7% of the sheet, so full-page) and the tall plate on sheet 16 (240x660pt, 56% of the column, under the full-page mark): each on one sheet only, so repetition cannot reach it and it must arrive as art. And a 200x100pt letterhead on all 17 sheets, the furniture rule at document scale, which must reach the book as nothing at all. tests/torture-pictures.test.ts asserts the four kept, all 17 refusals as furniture, and each note's width and full-page verdict. images.pdf refuses one picture by each of four rules (pixels, width, furniture, background), height and area are pinned only by hand-built candidates in tests/artwork.test.ts, and jpx.pdf owns the JPEG 2000 decoder. Picture files are named by PDF page, one more than the sheet: sheet 14's panel is p015-01.png
deviceChecks: the letterhead is nowhere in the book. Every sheet of the PDF carries the same 200x100pt logo in its bottom margin, and the book must show none of it: not on the title card's page, not under a scene, not at the end. If it appears even once, report the page it is on

nothing that was art is missing. The book shows four pictures: the title card at the front (by default as the book's cover rather than a page), the storyboard panel on sheet 14, the map plate on sheet 15 and the tall plate on sheet 16. A missing one is reported by its sheet

title: Pictures in the book (option, default ON)
how: the title card stands ahead of every scene heading with nothing before it but the title page block, so by default it is the book's cover (#19b) and on none of the pages; with promoteCoverImage off the book opens instead on an Opening section holding the card alone as a full-page figure (w100, figure-full). The panel on sheet 14 and the tall plate on sheet 16 stay in the flow at w40 and w55; and on sheet 15 a scene heading sits directly above the map plate, a full-page figure, with nothing between them. Asserted on the built EPUB by tests/torture-pictures.test.ts, and the book validates clean under epubcheck. What only a device can answer is listed under The pictures
deviceChecks: the storyboard panel on sheet 14 holds its width: a little under half the text column, centered, with its heading above it and the action below. Not a thumbnail, not full width, and nothing running off the right edge at any font size

a heading above a full-page plate. On sheet 15, INT. MAP ROOM - NIGHT sits directly above the map plate, whose break before overrides the heading's keep with what follows; in Chrome the heading ends its page alone. On the device: is the heading alone at the foot of a page, or carried onto the plate's page? Either answer is a verdict worth recording

a plate taller than the page. The tall plate on sheet 16 is 1:2.75 at the source and set at 55% of the text column, so on a 3:4 e-reader screen it runs past one page at any font size, and it is under the full-page mark on purpose so no forced break hides that. Chrome slices it across pages; whether the reader slices it, scales it to fit, or clips it is the question, and 'it scaled' is as useful a report as 'it broke'

WHILE THE .MOBI IS TEXT-ONLY (MOBI_CARRIES_PICTURES is false in src/mobi/html.ts, the default until the picture-size probe below passes), this check is only that torture.mobi appears in the library, opens, and shows no picture and no empty box where one would be. Once the gate is open, it is this: the engine's .mobi, sideloaded over USB (the file for the oldest Kindles, asked for by name). Build it from the repo root with `mkdir -p ~/Desktop/torture-check && bun src/cli.ts tests/fixtures/torture.pdf --mobi -o ~/Desktop/torture-check/torture.epub`, which writes torture.mobi, torture.fountain and the torture.images folder beside that EPUB and nothing into tests/fixtures (the folder has to exist first, since the CLI does not make it), then copy torture.mobi to the Kindle's documents folder. All four pictures are there and in their places: the title card first, the panel, the map plate, the tall plate. The device chooses their widths, since the .mobi cannot state a share of the column. A missing picture, an empty box, or one picture where another belongs is the failure

WHILE THE .MOBI IS TEXT-ONLY (MOBI_CARRIES_PICTURES is false in src/mobi/html.ts, the default until the picture-size probe below passes), this check is only that torture.mobi appears in the library, opens, and shows no picture and no empty box where one would be. Once the gate is open, it is this: the .mobi's full-page plates. The title card and the map plate each have a page to themselves: the card straight after the title page with no blank page in front, the map plate's heading ending its page alone above it, and the text after each plate starting a fresh page, never two page turns in a row

the picture size an older Kindle accepts in a .mobi. Build the probe (bun tools/mobi-picture-probe.ts --out <folder>) and copy all four .mobi files it writes to the Kindle's documents folder: method-reader-picture-probe.mobi, method-reader-picture-probe-2kb.mobi, method-reader-picture-probe-200kb.mobi and method-reader-picture-probe-1400kb.mobi. They appear as Picture Probe, Picture Probe 2 KB, Picture Probe 200 KB and Picture Probe 1.4 MB. Picture Probe holds all three pictures, one to a scene; each of the other three holds one of them alone, so if the largest makes the Kindle refuse a whole book, the smaller sizes still answer from books of their own. Each picture comes after a line naming its size (about 2 KB, about 200 KB, and about 1.4 MB as a full-page plate), and each is a black frame around a grey checkerboard with a patch of static. Record for each of the four books, and for each picture in it, whether the picture shows, shows as an empty box, or the book does not open or does not appear in the library. A failure is plausible: Calibre never writes a PNG into this format (every picture becomes a JPEG, or a GIF when it keeps originals), and Amazon's kindlegen capped pictures at 64 or 128 KB. If the 2 KB picture fails too, the cause is the PNG format rather than the size. The engine's .mobi stays text-only (MOBI_CARRIES_PICTURES in src/mobi/html.ts) until all four books open and every picture shows; if they do, that constant becomes true in one line. If any fails, it stays false

title: The title card as the cover (option, default ON)
how: the title card behind the title sheet is a full-page picture with nothing ahead of it but the title page block, so by default it is the book's cover. In the EPUB it is declared both ways (properties="cover-image" on its item and <meta name="cover">), drawn on none of the pages, and the body opens on its first scene as sc-001. In the .mobi, once its pictures are switched on (MOBI_CARRIES_PICTURES), EXTH 201 names its record (0) and the card is still drawn first, on a page of its own straight after the title page; until then the .mobi has neither. Asserted by tests/torture-pictures.test.ts, and the EPUB validates clean under epubcheck. What only a device can answer is listed under The pictures
deviceChecks: the cover in the library. Open the default book in Apple Books, copy its EPUB to a Kobo or tolino, and its KFX (or AZW3) to the Kindle's documents folder: each library shows the title card as the book's cover, not a grey or generated tile. On a newer Kindle (Colorsoft and later) Amazon deletes the covers of USB-sent books that are not Amazon's, so a plain tile there is a known Kindle behaviour rather than this book's fault: record the model, its firmware, and whether it had been online since the copy

the body opens on the first scene. The title card is the book's cover by default, so it is not a page of the body: the first scene heading, INT. ARCHIVE BASEMENT - NIGHT, comes straight after the generated title page, where Begin Reading lands. The card appearing as the first body page anyway, or a blank page where it used to stand, is the failure

the cover inside the book. Where the reader offers a way to the cover from inside the book (on a Kindle, Go To and then Cover), it shows the title card, whole and undistorted. On a Kindle that deleted the library tile this is the answer that matters: the cover is reported to survive inside the book

WHILE THE .MOBI IS TEXT-ONLY (MOBI_CARRIES_PICTURES is false in src/mobi/html.ts, the default until the picture-size probe below passes), this check is only that torture.mobi appears in the library, opens, and shows no picture and no empty box where one would be. Once the gate is open, it is this: the .mobi shows the card twice, on purpose. Copy torture.mobi from the #19a .mobi check to the Kindle's documents folder: the library shows the title card as its cover (subject to the deletion above), and the book still has the card on a page of its own straight after the title page, because the .mobi keeps it there. Record both answers separately: the card as the cover but missing from its page, or on its page but not the cover, is the finding; seeing it in both places is the intended result. First of all, the book must appear in the library and open. If it does not while the picture probe books do, copy torture-check-nocover/torture.mobi (from the next check) too: if that one appears and opens, the cover record is the cause, and the .mobi drops its cover record rather than its pictures

no blank page before a front plate, which the default EPUB no longer has, since its card is the cover. Build the book with the cover off, from the repo root: `mkdir -p ~/Desktop/torture-check-nocover && bun src/cli.ts tests/fixtures/torture.pdf --mobi --options-json '{"promoteCoverImage":false}' -o ~/Desktop/torture-check-nocover/torture.epub`, which writes torture.epub, torture.mobi, torture.fountain and the torture.images folder there and nothing into tests/fixtures. For the Kindle, make its KFX or AZW3 from that EPUB with Method Reader's Save a Kindle file, or copy that torture.mobi. Read the EPUB on the Kobo or tolino and the Kindle file on the Kindle: the title card is the first page of the body, on a page of its own straight after the generated title page, as wide as the text column or as large as the page allows, and the first scene heading starts on the next page. A blank page between the title page and the card is the failure. Verified in Chrome only

title: Method Reader's own AZW3 (beta)
how: the whole fixture as an AZW3 Method Reader writes itself, with no Calibre: every scene, both dual exchanges, the four pictures and the title card as its cover. Build it from the repo root with `mkdir -p ~/Desktop/torture-check && bun src/cli.ts tests/fixtures/torture.pdf --azw3 ~/Desktop/torture-check/torture.azw3 -o ~/Desktop/torture-check/torture.epub` and copy torture.azw3 to the Kindle's documents folder. tests/azw3.test.ts reads it back structurally and tests/azw3-calibre.test.ts through Calibre's own reader; what only a device can answer is under Method Reader's own AZW3
deviceChecks: it is a book. torture.azw3 appears in the library within a minute of the copy, titled The Proof Sheet, and opens. Not appearing, appearing as a document with no cover, or not opening is the failure, and the first thing to report

the cover. The library shows the title card as the book's cover, and Go To, then Cover, shows it inside the book. On a Kindle that deletes covers of USB-sent books (Colorsoft and later), record the model and firmware and answer from inside the book

where it opens and how it moves. A first open lands on the first scene, INT. ARCHIVE BASEMENT - NIGHT, past the generated title page; Go To lists every scene heading in order, and choosing one lands on it. Close the book on a later page and open it again: it comes back to that page

the pictures. The storyboard panel, the map plate and the tall plate all show, each where the KFX shows it. The AZW3 keeps them as PNGs, which kindlegen never wrote; a missing picture or an empty box is the failure, and which one

the layout the stylesheet asks for. The dialogue column sits indented from both sides, cues centered over it, and both dual dialogue exchanges read as two columns side by side. Keeps are not a finding here: the KF8 renderer ignores them (registry #8b), so a cue at the foot of a page is expected
